facts.text: Amantaka is at 55/3 Kingkitsarath Road, Ban Thongchaleun, Luang Prabang, Laos.
The drive from Luang Prabang International Airport to Amantaka is 10 minutes.
Amantaka sits beneath Mount Phousi, a stroll from the riverbank and the town's main street.
facts.excerpt: Beneath sacred Mount Phousi, just a stroll from the riverbank and the town’s bustling main street, Amantaka is a serene base for exploring Luang Prabang’s many attractions.

facts.text: The resort takes its name from Tipitaka, meaning 'the teaching of Buddha'.
facts.excerpt: Taking its name from Tipitaka, meaning ‘the teaching of Buddha’

facts.text: The resort has a swimming pool and a spa.
facts.excerpt: the resort with its shimmering swimming pool, expansive spa and genteel ambience

facts.text: Amantaka is in Luang Prabang, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, at the foot of Mount Phousi amid golden spired wats and quaint lanes.
facts.excerpt: Amantaka rests at the foot of sacred Mount Phousi amid the golden spired wats and quaint lanes of this charming UNESCO World Heritage Site.

facts.text: The property is a conversion of Luang Prabang's old provincial hospital.
facts.excerpt: A clever conversion of Luang Prabang’s old provincial hospital

facts.text: The colonial-style lobby, under a low red-tiled roof, is the former X-ray room.
facts.excerpt: A sweeping driveway brings guests to a colonial-style lobby (the former X-ray room) beneath a low-slung red-tiled roof.

facts.text: The suites surround a garden and a pool.
facts.excerpt: Twenty-four cream suites surround a shady centerpiece garden and expansive pool.

facts.text: The bigger suites have private pools.
facts.excerpt: Smaller suites are more cozy; the bigger ones have private pools.

facts.text: Decor uses simple Southeast Asian wood furnishings, an embroidered silk throw and black-and-white photographs of Buddhist monks in meditation.
facts.excerpt: simple Southeast Asian wood furnishings, an embroidered silk throw, black-and-white photographs of Buddhist monks in meditation

facts.text: The town's experts in Theravada Buddhism, traditional arts and ethnology are on call for guests.
facts.excerpt: On call are the town’s experts in Theravada Buddhism, traditional arts, and ethnology

facts.text: Guests get access to a photographic archive of monastic life dating back to the 1880s.
facts.excerpt: exclusive access to, for example, a photographic archive of monastic life dating back to the 1880s

facts.text: A member of the former royal family is on hand to discuss Lao fine arts.
facts.excerpt: A member of the former royal family is on hand to discuss Lao fine arts

facts.text: Guided walks lead away from the main sights to explore abandoned temples.
facts.excerpt: there are guided walks away from the main sights to explore abandoned temples

facts.text: The interior is pared down to the point of austere, in contrast to the town's gilded temples.
facts.excerpt: Inside, it’s pared down to the point of austere, but in a soothing contrast to this tropical town of gilded temples and extravagant carvings.

facts.text: The hotel has a slight sanitarium feel, with long corridors and tiny ward-like chambers.
facts.excerpt: the hotel has a slight sanitarium feel, with long corridors and tiny ward-like chambers

facts.text: Called the most luxurious property in the country.
facts.excerpt: has created the most luxurious property in the country
